expo.name: Scanified
//platforms: Two, not three. With no `platforms` key Expo defaults to ios, android AND
web, and `eas update` exports every platform in that list. The first OTA
this project ever tried to publish died in the export step asking for
react-native-web - a dependency for a target that does not exist. This app
is a handset app; there is no web build and there never was one.
runtimeVersion does not move with every app version bump - only bump it
when a native/JS change would break OTA compatibility with what's already
It moved 1.2.2 -> 1.2.3 for a second reason, and this one is worth
remembering. An OTA published to the production channel for runtime 1.2.2
carried the launch crash - the navigate-before-mount bug documented in
app/_layout.tsx. Store builds 208 and earlier also declare runtime 1.2.2,
so a phone running a FIXED binary would still download that broken bundle
on launch and crash anyway; the embedded fix would never get a chance.
Bumping the runtime is what strands the bad bundle: nothing asks for
1.2.2 any more, so nothing is served it. Disabling updates outright would
also have worked and would have cost the fleet OTA permanently.
Do not lower this back to 1.2.2.
